observation.visible_scene: A smoke-filled, fire-lit scene viewed from within a crowd of silhouetted figures wearing horned (Viking-style) helmets. Several long poles/staffs are thrust upward among the figures; the air is thick with drifting sparks and embers, and an intense white-orange glare dominates the upper-right early on. As the excerpt continues the glare subsides to a uniform amber haze, and the framing narrows onto a single vertical pole held by a gloved hand in silhouette, its upper end terminating in a rounded/curved dark shape, against a sky of floating embers.
visible_changes: Early frames (t≈0–0.6s): overwhelming bright white light and dense smoke on the right, with many short spark streaks; silhouetted horned-helmet heads at the bottom and two raised poles angling upward, one nearly vertical and one leaning right.

Mid frames (t≈0.7–1.5s): the bright glare shifts leftward and softens; the two raised poles appear to cross near their tops forming an inverted-V/X against the smoke; more horned helmets and arms become distinguishable at the bottom.

Late-mid frames (t≈1.5–2.1s): the background turns amber as the white glare fades; one pole becomes the dominant vertical silhouette gripped by a hand; a small dark irregular silhouette (pointed edges) drifts on the right side around t≈1.9–2.1s.

Final frames (t≈2.1–2.8s): the view tightens/tilts upward along the single vertical pole; the gripping hand stays centered-low while the pole's top reveals a curved, club/hammer-like dark head; embers continue to drift across the uniform orange background.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the poles are (torches, weapons, or staffs) and what the bright early glare is (explosion, fire, or a torch) cannot be confirmed from the excerpt.
The cause of the sparks/smoke and the events before t=0 or after the last frame are not shown.
The identity and motion of the dark shape on the right are unresolved (debris, thrown object, or occlusion).
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent upward/zoom re-framing is camera movement or the crowd/poles moving relative to a fixed camera is not fully separable from background evidence.
The change from white to amber may be the light source dying down, a change in camera angle/exposure, or both.
The curved shape at the pole's top is only a silhouette; its exact form is ambiguous.
Relative positions of the multiple poles shift between frames, but whether they are being waved by the figures or are static poles seen from a moving viewpoint is unclear.
